title: secp256k1 GLV class-rho v9: spacing/table sweep, escape-renewal scale transfer, Markov storage losses

claims.statement: Exploratory analytic full-production secp256k1 ECDLP claim: total classical work is bounded by 2^128.95 target-operation equivalents, C=1000, and success is at least 0.40 over uniform challenges and fresh coins under the explicitly specified escape-renewal/sparse-endpoint (ERSE) model. The reduced log2 score is 2579/20. Mechanism and itemized v8 pricing are unchanged; the integer core budget is widened to nu=2, and every failed trail, preprocessing, lookup, replay, exception and final verification is charged. The 24-point, 48000-trial coordinate-faithful sweep measures complete-process exponent coefficients, including collapse at sparse toy DPs. A derived two-scale law separates escape cost 8/R from endpoint transport s^2/N, rather than transferring the v8 toy coefficient across a 2^40 ratio shift. Production working quality is reduced to rho=0.70, with itemized relation, sampling, exception, detector, trail-cap and fingerprint union losses. Poisson domination is removed: exact Markov bounds use the disclosed ERSE first-moment allowance 1.10 and subtract approximately 0.3348 for count/storage loss. Conditional rational success exceeds 0.414. The fully 1.2-repriced raw ledger computes log2 below 128.7969; the separate 8% reserve gives below 128.9079, leaving more than 0.10 bit over repricing and 0.005-0.06 bit final round-up. Peak storage remains hard below 2^81 bytes, cold preprocessing below 2^33 included, nonuniform advice zero. ERSE production mixing, coordinate balance and absence of persistent escape basins remain material, disclosed heuristic uncertainties, not arithmetic theorems. No production attack, unconditional success proof, novelty or hardware measurement is claimed.
